claimCounting: Current independent pass: 88 lesson propositions in claimInventory, 18 complete question reviews including every key/distractor/feedback, 54 glossary definitions and aliases, 12 analogy mapping/limitation checks, and one retained formula. Source choices and two executable models checked separately; editorial formula removal is not counted as an accuracy correction.
corrections: The lesson phrase processor exception resolved to an OS definition limited to instruction-caused faults. Added the embedded Cortex-M exception meaning, including device interrupts, with a local alias; preserved all existing glossary IDs.

Setup and hold time cited the SPI API header, which does not explain its timing margins. Replaced its source with the RP2040 datasheet sections describing sampling and selection setup/hold requirements.
gaps: No real RP2040 execution, ISR installation/acknowledgement, measured interrupt latency, DMA concurrency or electrical waveform tests. Host models validate C logic and saved-state behavior only; SDK instructions and hardware claims were source-reviewed.

Fictional I2C/SPI examples deliberately provide their own command contracts. Actual sensor registers, resistor sizing, multiple-controller arbitration and production bus recovery remain outside this introductory scope.

The UART lesson explains bounded partial parsing and resynchronisation policy without implementing a production parser; specific error recovery and throughput must be designed for the actual application.
Renderer, iPhone layout and offline checks are delegated to root integration; this record claims source/content and scoped build verification only.

primarySourceReview.scope: C11 6.2.5, 6.3.1.3 and 7.20.1.1; CMSIS pending/priority/exception/saturation; GCC volatile and atomic implementation restrictions; Pico save/restore calling-core scope, UART framing/FIFOs, SPI format and completion, I2C seven-bit/timeout APIs, DMA and timer policies; NXP 3.1 protocol; RP2040 UART/SPI operation; TI electrical distinction; Arduino signal names.

Blocking calls can delay further observations.
Hardware condition requests exception; handler executes when accepted.
Pending state, masks, priorities and execution context affect acceptance.
An interrupt is not an instantaneous callback.
Bounded ISR work retains information, acknowledges source and defers expensive work.
NVIC pending-bit clearing and peripheral-source clearing can differ.
Reads at 0,5,10ms miss a pulse restricted to 1–2ms.
A latched request depends on configured peripheral semantics.
One pending indication can merge multiple events.
FIFO retention is finite.
Latest state, event count and every-byte retention are different requirements.
Worst check interval under actual driver/logging load matters, not average loop speed.
est-timers-nonblocking: Waiting can prevent other main-loop work.
Due checks let the loop continue between actions.
Abstract source is explicitly uint32 with one increment/ms, not hardware configuration.
uint32_t is optional exact-width unsigned32 when provided.
Unsigned counter rollover returns to zero.
Direct wrapped-deadline comparison can return the wrong result.
Conversion of subtraction back to uint32 recovers elapsed modulo2^32.
Integer promotions do not invalidate this subtraction-and-cast expression.
Actual elapsed must remain below one complete counter cycle.
Counter snapshots cannot reveal missed complete cycles.
Complete host C11 helper has deterministic output1.
UINT32_MAX-3 to6 is ten tick advances.

Restart at observed now shifts phase; fixed phase requires lateness policy.
Late work cannot be made punctual by arithmetic; check increment duration and loop delay.
est-isr-sharing: ISR can interleave a multi-instruction foreground operation.
Volatile does not imply indivisibility, thread synchronization or unrelated-memory ordering.
Boolean flag repeated stores merge arrivals.
Counter/queue requires capacity and overflow policy; hardware may already merge events.
Trace copy3/increment4/clear0 loses the fourth.
Short critical section excludes only specified competitors.

restore_interrupts restores saved PRIMASK, including previously disabled state.

Frame configuration does not establish voltage/pin compatibility.

Binary signalling numerical baud and bit rates coincide in this example.
96 bytes require960 line bits and0.1s at9600bits/s without gaps.
FIFO/software storage is finite and does not fix sustained producer-consumer imbalance.
Overrun loss and reporting depend on hardware/driver.
Newline and max command length are explicit application protocol rules.
Overlong commands need rejection/resynchronization policy.
O,N,newline completes only on terminator; arbitrary receive boundaries require partial state.
ISR waiting/interpretation should be bounded and deferred where possible.
est-i2c-basics: Ordinary bidirectional I2C uses SDA/SCL with pull-low/release and pullups.
Levels and pullups require actual board/device/bus specifications.
Lesson states one controller and seven-bit addressing.
I2C protocol does not define universal sensor registers.
Fictional target contract selects register01 and returns7A at seven-bit48.
Write address byte90/read91 combine address with direction.
Write pointer then repeatedSTART read has no interveningSTOP.
Receivers ACK preceding bytes; final receiver NACK ends requested data normally.
Address NACK has different context from normal final read NACK.
SDK accepts seven-bit address, not shifted wire byte.
ACK does not establish fresh application data or unique target identity.
Timeout operations and returned count/error must be checked.
Clock stretching is mode/device dependent.
Timeout bounds waiting but does not repair electrical faults.
Retry/recovery requires bounded deliberate policy.
est-spi-basics: Common four-signal SPI uses controllerclock, two directions and chipselect.
Both directions can shift at once although useful content can be one-way.
COPI/MOSI output and CIPO/MISO input direction labels are equivalent in this scope.
Electrical/pin-function compatibility must be checked using actual hardware.
CPOL describes idle; CPHA describes sampling position.
Mode0 idlelow/rising leading capture/falling subsequent change.
First data bit must be valid before first mode0 sampling edge.
Mode, bit order, transfer width and maximum rate are device requirements.
CS setup/hold and command framing are device-specific.
Slower clock does not change the selected sampling edge.
Fictional command+dummy contract uses one active-low selection and returnsstatussecond.
Completion must reach documented hardware-transfer point before releasing selection.
A generic transmit function may return after buffering; inspect concrete SDK semantics.
SPI has no universal I2C address/ACK phase.
Application response/status can require validation beyond clocking.
Unselected shared-return devices must release the wire per device specification.

est-polling-interrupts-q1.review: B: every observation lies outside the pulse; no latch is assumed.

est-polling-interrupts-q2.review: A/C/D: bounded preservation, capacity checks and device acknowledgement are appropriate; a pending flag cannot count bytes.

est-polling-interrupts-q3.review: C: one or more events can create the same true flag; neither exact count nor instantaneous service follows.

est-timers-nonblocking-q1.review: D: converting the difference to the unsigned width recovers the bounded forward count; it cannot count missed full cycles.

est-timers-nonblocking-q2.review: A: only the elapsed remainder is retained; signed interpretation cannot restore lost information.

est-timers-nonblocking-q3.review: B: restarting from late handling shifts future timing; catching up or fixed phase requires another policy.

est-isr-sharing-q1.review: C: copied three survives locally, the fourth increment is erased by clear.

est-isr-sharing-q2.review: D: restore the saved state, preserving an already-disabled caller.

est-isr-sharing-q3.review: A/C/D: flags merge arrivals, counters need bounds, and atomics require target checks; calling-core masking excludes no other core.

est-uart-basics-q1.review: A: start/stop bits are serial wire time; a larger buffer changes neither framing nor bit rate.

est-uart-basics-q2.review: A/B/D: bounded application framing, error handling/draining and partial state are required; matching baud does not establish electrical compatibility.

est-uart-basics-q3.review: B: preserve ON until the specified newline or a defined error/limit; read calls and byte frames do not complete the application command.

est-i2c-basics-q1.review: C: the Pico API requires 0x48, not the combined 0x90/0x91 wire byte or register selector.

est-i2c-basics-q2.review: D: the controller final-read NACK normally declines further bytes; it is neither address failure nor data freshness proof.

est-i2c-basics-q3.review: A/C: bound the operation and inspect/report failures; ACK does not prove freshness and unbounded retries block other work.

est-spi-basics-q1.review: A: data must be stable at the required sample edge; chip-select changes, blind confidence or lowering rate alone do not fix mode mismatch.

est-spi-basics-q2.review: B: keep selection over command and dummy transfer and collect status during the latter under the supplied fictional contract.

est-spi-basics-q3.review: B/C: response validation and device framing still matter; SPI provides neither I2C ACK nor unconditional shared-return release.

timer.result: All combinations of six start positions, ten elapsed distances and ten intervals passed, including zero, threshold neighbours, signed-boundary and UINT32_MAX values.

isr.result: Exact lesson fragment compiled with host SDK shim; six drains including empty/three/one events, initial mask enabled/disabled restoration and lost-event interleaving passed.
isr.limitation: Host shim does not execute real PRIMASK instructions, run concurrent ISR delivery or verify peripheral acknowledgement.

maths: 96 × 10 / 9600 = 0.1 seconds = 100 milliseconds under stated no-gap binary 8N1 assumptions.
UINT32_MAX minus three to six is ten forward tick increments modulo 2^32.
Seven-bit 0x48 becomes write wire byte 0x90 or read byte 0x91.
Reads at 0/5/10 ms all miss an active pulse from 1 to 2 ms.

analogyReview.scope: All six unchanged analogy blocks independently reread with technical text and questions; hashes renewed only after this review.
gaps: No real RP2040 execution, ISR installation/acknowledgement, measured interrupt latency, DMA concurrency or electrical waveform tests. Host models validate C logic and saved-state behavior only; SDK instructions and hardware claims were source-reviewed.

est-polling-interrupts.rationale: Door checks map repeated observation and a bell maps an interrupt request; explicit limits prevent assuming instantaneous handling or one retained indication per arrival. CMSIS and Pico IRQ source support pending/masking/acknowledgement distinctions.

est-timers-nonblocking.rationale: Mileage rollover maps a finite counter position and bounded forward difference. The limit correctly forbids recovering complete missed cycles; C unsigned conversion confirms the mapping. Tick duration and observation bound remain visible.

est-isr-sharing.rationale: Order-slip collection maps excluding the ISR during copy/clear and restoring the previous closed/open state. SDK PRIMASK helpers support this; the limit explicitly excludes other cores/hardware actors and lost events.

est-uart-basics.rationale: Letter tray maps finite storage and temporary tolerance of a servicing pause. RP2040 UART FIFO/overrun behavior supports the mapping. The limit explicitly distinguishes buffered bytes from complete application messages.

est-i2c-basics.rationale: Addressed letter/request/reply maps target selection and the explicitly fictional combined write/read. NXP protocol supports the repeated START mapping; precise ACK rules, command-specific meaning and duplicate addresses remain limitations.

est-spi-basics.rationale: Leader beat maps the supplied serial clock and agreed sampling edge. RP2040 SPI timing supports this; the limit explicitly excludes universal command syntax, timing details and proof of acceptance.

verificationHistory.claimCounting: Distinct review units: 88 listed lesson propositions;18 complete question reviews (each includes all four options, key and worked example);50 glossary definitions/aliases;12 analogy mapping/limitation reviews;2 complete formula cards. Repeated wording is not counted again.
corrections: ISR analogy said to reopen the hatch even when preserving a previously disabled state. It now restores its previous state and explicitly leaves an already closed hatch closed.

Generic Acknowledgement and target device glossary names could mislabel peripheral ISR acknowledgement or unrelated hardware as I2C. Renamed the former I2C acknowledgement (ACK retained) and removed the broad target device alias.

Broad saturation alias could capture unrelated concepts; replaced with saturating counter and used counter saturation in the lesson. DMA engine and full-duplex now resolve to the appropriate local entries.

Several automatic links used unrelated database transactions, lexical closure, C assertions, ADC resolution, CPU word size, MIDI status/data byte, syscall read/write, happens-before or API rate limits. Rephrased those occurrences with precise ordinary descriptions while preserving question IDs, keys and substantive technical meaning.

Wrapping-counter glossary reference pointed at a time API instead of C unsigned semantics; counter-saturation reference pointed at interrupt helpers instead of saturation; COPI/CIPO references did not establish those names. Replaced with exact C11, Arm saturation and official Arduino naming references.
UART worked substitution could ambiguously attach seconds to the denominator; grouped the numerical quotient before seconds in both standalone formula cards.
Bus connection advice specified actual device electrical compatibility but did not repeat the course low-voltage-only boundary. Added that visible boundary beside UART, I2C and SPI connection advice.
gaps: No physical board execution, measured interrupt latency, electrical waveform or bus-wiring validation. Host timer execution and PRIMASK model test logic only; no MMIO is executed.
ISR sketch deliberately covers only stated RP2040 single-core foreground/ISR assumptions. DMA implementations, multicore synchronization and lock-free structures remain beyond beginner scope.
I2C/SPI command contracts are expressly fictional; no actual sensor register map or universal command/CS timing is asserted.
Serial parser policy is explained and traced rather than shipped as a full production protocol stack; protocol resynchronization and recovery remain device/application-specific.

analogyReview.scope: Full independent review of all six new lessons, including complete technical content outside disclosures, all question content and glossary; not a heuristic-only analogy inventory.
corrections: ISR analogy said to reopen the hatch even when preserving a previously disabled state. It now restores its previous state and explicitly leaves an already closed hatch closed.
gaps: No physical board execution, measured interrupt latency, electrical waveform or bus-wiring validation. Host timer execution and PRIMASK model test logic only; no MMIO is executed.

est-polling-interrupts.rationale: Added door checking versus bell: maps explicit checks versus a retained request; limit explicitly covers masks, priority, acknowledgement and merged arrivals. No guarantee of one request per arrival.

est-timers-nonblocking.rationale: Added rolling mileage display: subtraction across displayed rollover is useful; limit explicitly rejects inferring complete missed cycles. Width, tick duration and strict actual-elapsed bound remain visible.

est-isr-sharing.rationale: Added order-slip hatch: closure maps exclusion during take-and-clear. Corrected restoration so an already closed hatch stays closed, matching saved disabled PRIMASK. Limit excludes other hardware actors and lost/overflowed events.

est-uart-basics.rationale: Added letter tray: finite capacity buys pause time but cannot fix sustained overload. Limit distinguishes byte buffering from complete application messages and error handling.

est-i2c-basics.rationale: Added addressed request/reply: selects recipient, writes pointer and changes direction within the stated combined exchange. Limit preserves precise clock/ACK rules and warns duplicate address acknowledgement does not identify a device.

est-spi-basics.rationale: Added beat leader: maps presentation and sampling to configured clock edges; chip selection marks exchange. Limit leaves electrical timing, bit order and command/acceptance semantics to the actual device.
